# `m.crypto.trades`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Trades of crypto pairs, tick by tick, from the exchanges Massive aggregates.

```python
m.crypto.trades(symbols)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `blink()`, `append_only()`, `ring()`, `last_by()`, `history()` |
| Served by | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| Time range | `start` and `end` are sent as `timestamp.gte` and `timestamp.lt` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Crypto pairs as Massive's tickers, such as `X:BTCUSD`, or `dm.ALL`, which `history()` reads only from the flat files. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and the rows of each one you delete leave the table. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Trades (flat files) | Trades (REST) | Trades (WebSocket) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Currencies Basic | Not included | Not included | Not included |
| Currencies Starter | End-of-day, All history | Real-time, All history | Real-time |
| Currencies Business | End-of-day, All history | Real-time, All history | Real-time |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST: the request's `cryptoTicker` parameter; flat files `ticker`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under."; WebSocket `pair`: "The crypto pair." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the row, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the UTC date of `Timestamp`. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's primary time, as an Instant. From REST `participant_timestamp`: "The nanosecond Exchange Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the trade was generated at the exchange."; flat files `participant_timestamp`: "The nanosecond accuracy Participant/Exchange Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the trade was actually generated at the exchange."; WebSocket `t`: "The Timestamp in Unix MS." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Price` | double | The price of the trade: the amount of the pair's second currency paid for one unit of its first (US dollars per bitcoin for X:BTCUSD). | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Size` | double | The size of a trade (also known as volume). | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Conditions` | long[] | A list of condition codes. See Crypto Condition Codes (https://massive.com/docs/rest/crypto/market-operations/condition-codes) for what each code means. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Exchange` | long | The exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/crypto/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Id` | String | The Trade ID which uniquely identifies a trade on the exchange that the trade happened on. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `ReceivedTimestamp` | Instant | The nanosecond accuracy timestamp of when the tick was received by Massive. | REST, WebSocket |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
